summary: Applies or removes Brown-Conrady lens distortion using radial, tangential, optical-center, focal-length, and layout controls.

key_params.name: invert
key_params.note: Approximate undistortion instead of applying distortion

key_params.name: k3
key_params.note: Third radial distortion coefficient; not used by inverse mode

key_params.name: center
key_params.note: Optical center components center1 and center2

key_params.name: extendmode
key_params.note: hold, zero, repeat, or mirror outside-source sampling

key_params.name: centeroffset
key_params.note: Shift distorted image within the output frame

common_gotchas: Inverse distortion is approximate and cannot recreate image content that was projected outside the frame.
k3 is not used by inverse distortion, even though it is part of the forward radial model.
Positive radial coefficients tend toward barrel/fisheye distortion; negative values tend toward pincushion distortion.
Optimal alpha and ROI crop choices can change output framing and resolution.
OpenCV calibration data must be mapped into the official center and focal-length units correctly.
key_concepts: Applies or approximates inverse Brown-Conrady lens distortion to TOP images.
Radial coefficients k1, k2, and k3 model barrel, fisheye, or pincushion distortion.
Tangential coefficients p1 and p2 compensate for off-axis lens/sensor alignment.
Optical center and focal length define the camera matrix used before distortion is applied.
Layout and post-transform controls preserve native detail, crop to ROI, or fit distorted content into the output frame.
Info CHOP channels expose optimal center, focal length, and ROI values for calibrated camera workflows.
